_meta.topic: State of BCI Security 2026: vulnerabilities, advisories, regulation, neurorights, incidents and research attacks, each classified validated or theoretical.

evidence_classes.validated: A disclosed CVE or advisory, a maintainer-acknowledged weakness, a published demonstration, a final court ruling, or a measured count.
evidence_classes.not_applicable: Laws, guidance and legal analysis: reported by legal status instead.

_meta.framing: Defensive. TARA and NISS are threat-modelling and risk-assessment tools. No item here describes how to carry out an attack.

demonstrated_case_without_neural_device_.attack: Phase dynamics replay/mimicry (GAN-synthesized or RF-injected neural trajectories)

items.title: Lab Streaming Layer transport has no encryption, authentication or integrity checking
items.reason: Maintainer-acknowledged design characteristic of a widely used neural-data streaming library; a mitigation (Secure LSL) is published. No CVE was assigned. Qinnovate raised the issue: disclose as a conflict of interest.

items.title: No mapped CVE appears in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
items.reason: Measured absence: 0 of 107 mapped CVEs in KEV v2026.10.20; CISA reports no known public exploitation for Pulsetto. Absence of recorded exploitation is not evidence of security.

items.title: No publicly confirmed malicious compromise of a BCI or neural-data product was found
items.reason: Search scope: NVD, CISA ICS medical advisories, KEV, web news for 2025-2026. One vendor-blog claim of a February 2026 CISA advisory naming three BCI makers could not be found at CISA and is excluded.

items.title: Supreme Court of Chile, Girardi v. Emotiv: consumer EEG data processed without valid consent
items.reason: Final court ruling; a privacy and consent finding, not a security breach.

items.title: Neurorights Foundation review of 30 consumer neurotech privacy policies
items.reason: Published systematic policy review with stated method; measures stated practice, not technical security.

items.title: P300 side channel leaks private information through consumer EEG
items.reason: Demonstrated in a lab study using inexpensive consumer EEG BCI devices (per the abstract).

items.title: Subliminal probing for private information with EEG-based BCIs
items.reason: Lab demonstration with human participants.

items.title: Wireless protocol of an implantable neurostimulator reverse-engineered
items.reason: Lab demonstration on real neurostimulator hardware; authors propose a countermeasure.

items.title: RF injection of false brain waves into a consumer EEG headset
items.reason: Lab demonstration that produced CVE-2023-49914.

items.title: Adversarial and backdoor attacks on EEG decoders
items.reason: Demonstrated on recorded EEG datasets (in silico). Validated as a decoder weakness; not demonstrated against a deployed clinical BCI.

items.title: Brainjacking: attack scenarios for implanted neuromodulation
items.reason: Review and threat analysis; scenarios are argued, not demonstrated on a neural implant in the paper.

items.title: Neurosecurity defined for neural devices
items.reason: Framing paper; no attack demonstration.

items.title: Cyber risks to next-generation BCIs and recommendations to regulators
items.reason: Analysis and recommendations (non-surgical updates, strong authentication, encryption, minimal connectivity); no new demonstration.

items.title: Five gaps in data protection for implantable BCIs under HIPAA and GDPR
items.reason: Legal and policy analysis; evidence class applies to threats, not to legal arguments.

items.title: FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance revised to align with the Quality Management System Regulation
items.reason: Regulatory status: final guidance in force. Section 524B premarket cybersecurity requirements apply to cyber devices since 2023-03-29.

items.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act vulnerability and incident reporting in force
items.reason: Regulatory status: in force. Inferred, not confirmed: consumer neurotech without a medical intended purpose falls under the CRA, while MDR medical devices are excluded.

items.title: EU AI Act high-risk deadlines postponed
items.reason: Regulatory status: Annex III 2027-12-02, Annex I 2028-08-02. Adoption reference not confirmed at EUR-Lex.

items.title: Five US states treat neural data as sensitive data; no federal law
items.reason: Enacted: Colorado, California, Montana, Connecticut, Vermont (Vermont effective 2028-01-01). Federal MIND Act introduced 2025-09-29, no action found.

items.title: UNESCO Recommendation (2025-11-12) and UN Secretary-General report A/81/351 (2026-10-15)
items.reason: Non-binding international instruments.
